key_insight: MFG trains an LLM to optimize molecules over multiple turns using feedback from earlier steps, improving both target properties and structural similarity.
engineering_relevance: This enables more practical drug-design pipelines by making iterative, similarity-constrained molecular optimization learnable rather than hand-crafted.
method: Reinforcement learning framework for multi-turn molecular optimization
Feedback vector encodes property gains and similarity to the source molecule
Feedback-aligned reward encourages progressive improvement across turns
evidence_signal: Evaluated on ten multi-objective molecular optimization tasks, where GeLLM3O-MFG achieved a highest average similarity-constrained success rate of 81.50% versus 70.81% for the base model.
watch_item: Performance depends on the quality of the feedback signal and reward design, so noisy or biased feedback could steer optimization in the wrong direction.
paper_title: MFG: Multi-turn Feedback Guided Molecular Optimization
